correctness_confidence.basis: All explicit rational identities in the PDF verify exactly: Eq. (1) V = 1011/50 and gap 11/2022, 5000/10161 and 30/61 under 9/epsilon jackpot scaling, Taylor residual 3772963/234881024, P(2/5)=447966/78125, P(1/4)=249075/8192, P(1/2)=141/32, Table 1 axiom counts (10 none, 8 propext+Quot.sound), and Table 2 totals (16 certs, 60/60 rejections). Full Lean theorem signatures are not printed in the PDF.

novelty.basis: The delegated-choice bounds, 5-item knapsack counterexample, Algorithm 2 capped menu, and Section 4 Bernstein polynomial split on [2/13, 2/5] and [2/5, 2/3] all originate from Abdi et al. [1]. The novelty lies strictly in the zero-dependency constructive Lean 4 kernel and the zero-float exact-Q certificate auditor DELEGATION-CERT-1.0.

reproducibility.basis: Names all source files, scripts, Lean version (4.35.0), SHA-256 tracking across 41 artifacts, and exact rational witnesses, enabling straightforward verification with the repo; however, the PDF omits the actual Lean theorem signatures, Proposition 3.3 branch payoffs, and exact distributions/parameters of the P4, C4, and 4-item knapsack instances.

rigor.basis: Zero-floating-point arithmetic, constructive Lean 4 proofs free of Classical.choice, sorry, and Lean.ofReduceBool, exact homogeneous Bernstein positivity, and a 60-case adversarial forgery suite provide high rigor within the stated scope. Main limitation is that Lean type signatures and proofs are summarized rather than shown in the 4-page PDF.

significance.basis: Provides a clean, machine-checked finite-rational and Bernstein-positivity verification artifact for combinatorial delegated choice, though impact is bounded by explicitly excluding the continuous stop-loss integrals (Sections 6-9) and large-scale LP infeasibility dual (Section 10) of Abdi et al. [1].

potential_errors: On page 1 Eq. (1), the jackpot payoff is written for fixed epsilon = 1/100 as (1/100)*900, whereas the epsilon in {1/50, 1/200, 1/1000} and epsilon -> 0 claims on page 3 (giving 5000/10161 and limit 30/61) implicitly require jackpot payoff 9/epsilon rather than 900.
The manuscript cites 5011/10110 (Proposition 1.1) and 0.48105 (Appendix A / Fig. 1b) without displaying the underlying randomized branch payoffs or LP dual values inside the PDF.
Figure 1(b) rounds 0.48105 to four decimal places as 0.4810 (round-half-to-even) while the text reports 0.48105.
strengths: Exact arithmetic and algebraic consistency across the PDF: Eq. (1) V = 1011/50, deterministic gap 11/2022, asymptotic 5000/10161 -> 30/61 (with 9/epsilon jackpot), Taylor certificate 3772963/234881024, and boundary evaluations P(2/5)=447966/78125, P(1/4)=249075/8192, and P(1/2)=141/32 all check out exactly.

Transparent and honest scope delineation: explicitly excludes continuous-distribution stop-loss integrals (Sections 6-9) and the Section 10 LP infeasibility dual rather than overclaiming end-to-end mechanization of [1].

Clean zero-dependency constructive Lean 4 kernel design (10 zero-axiom theorems, 8 using only [propext, Quot.sound], 0 Classical.choice, 0 sorry) paired with a pure-stdlib zero-float exact-Q auditor and 60-case adversarial forgery suite.
Internal consistency across text, Table 1 (18 theorems, 10 none / 8 [propext, Quot.sound]), Table 2 (16 certificates, 60/60 rejections, 0.050-1.077 ms), and Figures 1-3.
summary: This 4-page manuscript presents a machine-checked Lean 4 formalization kernel (18 constructive theorems, 10 zero-axiom and 8 using only [propext, Quot.sound], with 0 Classical.choice and 0 sorry) and a pure-stdlib zero-float exact-rational verifier (DELEGATION-CERT-1.0) covering the finite rational, knapsack impossibility, menu-score, and Section 4 Bernstein-positivity core of Abdi et al. (arXiv:2611.33095). All explicit rational identities, Taylor margins, polynomial evaluations, and table/figure summaries visible in the PDF are internally consistent and algebraically exact, and the authors transparently scope out the continuous stop-loss integrals (Sections 6-9) and Section 10 LP dual. The primary limitations are modest standalone mathematical novelty (verifying known results from [1]) and the omission of actual Lean theorem signatures, Eq. (1) general-epsilon jackpot scaling 9/epsilon, and benchmark distribution definitions from the short PDF.
weaknesses: Lean 4 theorem type signatures and formal definitions (e.g., downward-closed families, b_M(x), and universal rational quantification in Theorems 13-14) are summarized in prose rather than printed in the PDF, preventing self-contained verification of formal-statement fidelity from the manuscript alone.

The parameterization of Eq. (1) for general epsilon (9/epsilon jackpot value), the randomized Proposition 3.3 payoffs yielding 5011/10110, the reduction from Gamma(mu_0, b) to P(b), and the exact distributions/parameters for P4, C4, and the 4-item knapsack are not explicitly written out in the text.

The hardest analytic components of Abdi et al. [1] (continuous stop-loss integrals in Sections 6-9 and the Section 10 LP infeasibility dual) remain unformalized, limiting the scope of the verification.
